title: c34's Marangoni rods under a PhySim-style apparatus: no effect of dynamics noise is resolvable up to sd 0.01 per sqrt(t) in plain additive form or 0.03 in a physical form (conserved phi, proportional surfactant and cargo), and two probe arrays tell the world from its two active-stress ablations by an energy-score ratio of 6-80x within 15-150 t, but from the wall ablation (kappa=0) only at 15 and 50 t (3.1x, 1.8x), not at 150 t
summary:
Eval-readiness battery, second world (after 20261028T1330-c00-evalready-pm-noise-detect). Question: does a collective world keep its behaviour under the dynamics noise a PhySim evaluation needs, and can PhySim-style probe arrays see its deciding mechanisms? World: c34's nematic Marangoni rods, unchanged at its defaults (mar=40, kappa=20, chis=5, zeta=0.8, dt=0.05, 128^2, periodic). A wrapper (files/mg_noise.py) adds noise before every step; sd is per sqrt(t), so the per-step sd is 0.224 x sd. Two forms: plain (additive on phi, q1, q2, s and c) and physical (conserved divergence noise on phi, normalised to the same per-pixel sd; additive on q1 and q2; proportional on s and c).

**Noise dose-response (labkit packs to T=500, seeds 0-1, measured with c34's own scripts through files/measure.py; files/noise_table.json).**
- Baseline (same wrapper, sd 0): 14/11 persistent splits, generation 3/3, 4/2 swim-then-divide tracks, ring 100%, cargo in/out 12.43/12.43, daughters 100% at >= 2, speed 0.866/0.837 px per frame. On seed 0 the claim's record track (7.09 body lengths) is reproduced exactly. files/sheet_base_0_s0.png: droplets at t=45-110, rods by t=110-130, about 28 curved rods by t=500. The battery runs to half the claim's horizon; the claim reports 22/28 persistent splits at T=1000.
- Physical form, sd 0.003-0.03: 13-16 persistent splits, generation 2-4, 2-5 swim-then-divide tracks, ring 99-100%, daughters 100%. Cargo in/out drifts down 0-12% (11.77 to 10.98 on seed 0, 12.41 to 11.74 on seed 1) and speed varies by -18% to +5%. With one realisation per seed, no effect is resolvable: in an independent re-run the seed-2 baseline has cargo 11.14, about 10% below seeds 0-1, and its physical sd 0.01 run differs from it by -3% in speed and cargo (15 against 17 persistent splits). files/sheet_phys_0.01_s0.png matches the baseline sheet until about t=110, then the rod layout diverges; the rods stay clean and curved.
- Physical form, sd 0.1: degraded, structure intact. Persistent splits 10/12, merge/split 0.65/0.41, cargo 7.67/7.75 (-38%), daughters 97%/95%, ring 99%, speed 0.84/0.90. files/sheet_phys_0.1_s0.png: grainy bath, clean rods, already present at t=85 (baseline about 110).
- Plain form, sd 0.003-0.01: 14-17 persistent splits, generation 2-4, 2-4 swim-then-divide tracks, daughters 100%; cargo 11.0-11.63 (down 6-12%), speed -12% to +10%. Within the seed spread, so no effect is resolved.
- Plain form, sd 0.03: degraded. Cargo 7.71/8.11 (-36% on average), rim/out 9.38/9.27 against 11.1, merge/split 0.31/0.39, speed 1.07/1.01 (+23%/+21%), persistent splits 10/14, daughters 100%/97%.
- The levels that destroy the behaviour (plain 0.1, physical 0.3) are in 20261028T1610-c00-evalready-marangoni-breakers. With nonzero noise that leaves about one decade, 0.003-0.03 per sqrt(t), in the physical form. Its roughly 3x gain over the plain form mainly reflects removing the two clipped additive sources (the world clips s and c at zero); the size of the gain depends on how the conserved noise is normalised.

**Detectability (files/apparatus.py detect and score).** Prepared state: native world, seed 0, run noise-free to t=300: 19 rods, median area 51 px, half-width 2.24 px (files/prep_s0.json, files/prep_s0.png). Two probe arrays shaped like PhySim's devices: a 13-node square lattice at spacing 3 px on the target rod's deepest pixel and a 19-node hex lattice at spacing 6 px on another rod. Each node reads phi, q1, q2, s, c, vx and vy, plus each field's global mean and variance: 238 features per readout, every 2 t. Eight members per arm under physical-form noise of sd 0.01, every arm branched from the same native prepared state. Ratio = energy score of the native forecast against the arm's members / against an independent native ensemble, with every feature scaled by the native ensemble's pooled sd as in the pilot (files/score_s0_phys0.01_w150.json). At 15 / 50 / 150 t:
- mar=0 (Marangoni stress off): 16.9 / 22.5 / 14.8. By group: device0 31.0 / 23.6 / 7.9, device1 7.5 / 22.1 / 20.0, global 39.9 / 20.3 / 6.1. var(vx)+var(vy) falls 3x (time mean 0.0272 to 0.0092).
- Passive twin (zeta=0, mar=0): 14.9 / 19.9 / 12.8. By group: device0 26.8 / 24.8 / 16.4, device1 6.2 / 7.3 / 5.8, global 65.1 / 79.4 / 58.6. The flow stops; by t=150 the global variances of c and s are 6.6x and 11x the native ones.
- kappa=0 (wall off): 3.1 at 15 t (null band 0.96-1.04) and 1.8 at 50 t (null band 0.89-1.11). At 150 t it is not detectable from the probes or from all features (device0 1.48, device1 1.50, all 1.58; null bands 0.57-1.78 for device0 and 0.64-1.62 for all non-c features). Only the global group (2.1) still separates. Cargo acts back on nothing, so under kappa=0 phi, Q, s and v follow the native distribution exactly; their per-field ratios of 0.9-2.0 at 150 t are the noise floor of an 8-member ratio. The c field group scores 25.9 / 5.0 / 1.0.
- Post-hoc scores, chosen after seeing that the wall acts only on c (files/score_extra_s0_phys0.01_w150.json): the global cargo variance alone gives 119 / 44 / 19.4 for kappa=0, and the global sensor with each readout scaled by the native sd at that time gives 66.9 / 38.1 / 22.8. At t=150 the global cargo variance is 0.0045 under kappa=0 against 0.257 +- 0.009 (member sd) in the native ensemble.
limits:
- One world. Noise battery: 2 seeds, one realisation per seed and level, T=500 (half the claim's T=1000). A third seed was run only at sd 0 and physical sd 0.01, by the independent check. The spread between realisations was not measured directly; between seeds it is about 10% in cargo in/out.
- Swim-then-divide counts are 2-5 per seed, too few to resolve dose effects below the destroying level; those are judged by cargo in/out, rim/out, merge/split and speed. The best track on seed 0 drops from 7.09 to 3.7-5.8 body lengths at every nonzero level, including 0.003. The record track is a single trajectory, so I do not read this as weaker swimming, but that was not tested.
- The noise forms are my choice. The physical form changes three things at once: it removes both clipped additive sources (s and c become proportional) and makes the phi noise conserved. Normalising the conserved noise to the additive form's per-pixel sd is an arbitrary choice. Square-root (chemical-Langevin) noise on s and c was not tried.
- Detectability used one prepared state (seed 0, t=300), one probe placement, dilation 1, 128^2 only, one noise level (physical sd 0.01), 8 members per arm and windows up to 150 t (the nominal 15 t window is 8 readouts, 16 t). No injection was combined with detection.
- The ablated arms start from the native prepared state with the mechanism switched off at t=0 (under kappa=0 the global cargo variance is already 0.0103 at t=2, against 0.0859 native). The ratios therefore measure the response to switching a mechanism off, not the ablated world from its own prepared state, which is presumably how a hidden ablated world would start in PhySim.
- Deciding controls not run as detectability arms: the ring ablation (chis=0, the claim's B control) and the zeta=0, mar=40 twin.
- The kappa=0 verdict depends on feature scaling: pooled scaling gives 1.6-3.1x, the cargo-variance feature or per-time scaling 19-119x. Both of the latter were chosen after seeing the result and are not PhySim's fixed scoring. Per-time scaling divides by an 8-member sd that is tiny at early readouts, because all members start from one state. Only ratios are meaningful.
- The null bands are from the independent check's permutation null: 24 interchangeable members (native, truth, and kappa=0 with the c features removed), 300 random splits into forecast, reference and test, 5-95% bands. They cover all non-c features and device0, not every group. At 150 t the band is wide and its width depends on how features are scaled within each split.
- Ratios fall from 50 to 150 t partly because the native members diverge. One phi pulse of amp 1e-4 grows by about one e-fold per 21-24 t: that shows sensitive dependence on one state, not a Lyapunov estimate.
- The machine was shared with another agent.

finding.operator: robustness of reproduction, ring and cargo to dynamics noise of two forms, and visibility of the deciding mechanisms to PhySim-style probe arrays
finding.control: labkit packs on seeds 0-1 (T=500) at sd 0, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03 and 0.1 per sqrt(t) for plain additive and physical noise (conserved phi, additive Q, proportional s and c), seed 2 at sd 0 and physical 0.01 in an independent check; 8-member ensembles from a t=300 state under physical sd 0.01, native vs mar=0, passive twin (zeta=0, mar=0) and kappa=0, probe arrays of 13 and 19 nodes plus global mean and variance, against a permutation null
finding.result: no effect resolvable at plain sd <= 0.01 or physical sd <= 0.03 (cargo in/out down 0-12%, within a seed spread of about 10%); degraded at plain 0.03 and physical 0.1; energy-score ratio 14.8-22.5x for mar=0 and 12.8-19.9x for the passive twin at 15-150 t (6-80x in every sensor group); kappa=0 3.1x at 15 t and 1.8x at 50 t (null bands 0.96-1.04 and 0.89-1.11) and 1.6x at 150 t, inside the null band

implications: For PhySim evaluations of collective worlds: (1) the noise form matters here too, but through which field is clipped. Plain additive noise on the clipped cargo is harmless to the dynamics only because cargo is passive, which is why plain sd 0.01 per sqrt(t) is tolerated here while it killed phase_membrane; this is not general robustness to noise, and absolute sd values are not comparable across worlds with different field scales. (2) In the physical form the world keeps about one decade of noise (0.003-0.03 per sqrt(t)) with nonzero member spread and no resolvable damage, so the energy score has something to calibrate against. (3) Plain probe readouts see the two active-stress mechanisms at 6-80x within 15 t, in every sensor group. (4) A mechanism that acts only on a passive channel (the cargo wall) is diluted by an all-feature score and is lost in the noise by 150 t. A world contract should declare per-mechanism readouts or score groups before scoring (here the global cargo variance), not pick them after seeing results. (5) In this world short windows (15-50 t) separate better than long ones. Next: run the chis=0 and zeta=0, mar=40 arms; start each ablated arm from its own prepared state; add realisations per seed; fix the score groups in advance.
notes: Operator (c00) experiment for the PhySim eval-readiness line. An independent checker reviewed the battery; its corrections are applied here (kappa=0 at 150 t inside the null band, the chis=0 control not run, the dose-response wording, the post-hoc scores, ablations branched from the native state). files/recheck_* are the checker's seed-2 re-run. Packs were regenerated from files/mg_noise.py and files/runpack.sh; frames.npz and the detect ensembles (det_*.npz) are not committed. Compute includes the 128^2 battery, prep, the detect ensembles and the checker's re-run; the 64^2 screens and the pulse map are counted in the companion negative.
